lets can frame Evolution as nature's attempt to answer the not so trivial question: optimization of a blackbox, expensive to evaluate function, with a huge number of possible interactions and search space.
Let's imagine life as a function F(x,env).
x -> the individual. (possible space is estimated at 2^(9^10) for all possible creatures, each have at max ~10^17 possible parameters)
env - universe quantum state at this monument. most of it won't matter, but the full state is passed, because as time passes everything might interact with anything.
lets defined this in the simplest way possible:
The question is NOT max(F(x,env)) - how to have as many children as possible. Rather, it's closer to max(Y(x)):
The question is more like how to keep F(x,env) over time. and remember, life is about trade off.

That's the reason the r-strategy with maximizing children didn't work: the more resources you put to each child, the more the chance to not die too quickly and succeed. To put it simply, it's entirely possible to have a million children and none of them survive, because they don't have food.
Also, if you notice something about this integral - it takes care of all individuals.
Therefore it doesn't care about every single individual, just about the collective: some rabbits have no children at all, and a penguin might die when it's required for the collective.
I think the main reason people doesn't like to talk about evolution is pushback from WWII, when it was one of Germany main core ideologies.
Another reason could be that simply its better *even from evolution standpoint* to not know evolution. everything that we evolve with :
care for older people and other people, believe that humans are better then animals and other forms of life, everything is now in q.
So knowlage in evolution might make you question things like moral and eventually harder to find a meaning and help the group your in. or it might just be that people dont like changes.

welcome to the intro rectangle. each intro here is from a different field. hope you enjoy it
(look at the intro on arxiv.org/html/2604.22453v1) optimal transport
note: mathematicians in this field have an abstraction for a function or a pile of dirt : They call it a probability distribution

It makes some sense: if you send your hand and catch random dirt from a dirt pile, the dirt you end up with would have the same probability distribution as the height of the pile (the higher the pile the more likely it is to be chosen).
it's also incredibly annoying, since those probability distributions might have nothing to do with probability, it leaves you wondering what the probability distribution of a circle is.
anyway, optimal transport is the fancy way to find the optimal (minimize cost) way to transport from a pile of dirt to a known shape.
One day, RA noticed he had a problem. he ran a carrot delivery program. There were mainly four locations he needed the carrots to go to. the park (A),the garden (B) , the hill (C) and the pool (D)

On that day, the status was this: A:3,B:2, and he needed to deliver 1 to C and 4 to D. and he thought a lot about this: from where should he bring the missing carrots (so he could sleep instead of walking extra steps) ?
wouldn't it be nice if there was a formula that took the distances and calculates the fastest way?
so he started thinking . he started with the one carrot at C. it was easy to see it needed to come from the closest place to C, which in this case is A.

after that it was easy for him to see a mathematical formula: he assigned each way its "cost", how many steps. then he calculated every possible way and found out he must take 11 steps. 1(1)+4(2)+2(0)+1(2)=11
This was a massive success, which was a disaster for RA, more business meant more movement , meaning he couldn't sleep.

It was so successful that they asked every rabbit to submit its request for carrots at 8:00 AM. While looking at the submissions RA noticed something: most of them were predictable. and if he could predict the future well enough,
well, he could plan the routes and the amounts much better.
So, he adopted a new method. he started from the end of the week.
about 50% of the weeks, there is a party in the pool. on the other half, it rained. so if there was going to be a party, wouldn't it be better to bring carrots to D beforehand if the sky looks nice?

He changed his program to accept not only amount of carrots and locations, but also the current weather. it calculates the right amount, predicting what might be needed and where, not only now but in the future.
RA is a very smart and very lazy rabbit. He is the richest rabbit to date. There are rumors that he was a high-school girl that a magician transformed into a rabbit.
(look at the intro https://arxiv.org/html/2110.06870v2) Repurposing Discarded Smartphones
RA had always loved his phone. he found it once in the city, he learned how to write simple math programs on it and had used it on multiple occasions for route calculations..
At that time, the delivery company only had one phone. so whenever they needed a new route plan, they came to RA and it disturbed him while sleeping.
So what if every rabbit could have a phone? Buying them wasnt an option, he knew humans like to get colorful papers in the shop, and he had none of those.
"Also," he thought. "We don't need the best phone, just a simple one that can do math.".
so he searched what happened to the phones.
'~1.5B phones sold every year'. he had to read it three times to make sure he had read the number correctly.
"what?? ~1.5B phones per year? it couldn't be one per person, since just ~150m people are born each year. Do they eat them?
He searched for a while to find a human that eats phones. after a while, he chose a phone and decided to track it.
after about two years the owner bought a new phone, and put the phone in the drawer.
after about four years there, the owner put that phone into an electronics recycling bin.

did the phone die? RA's phone was about eight years old at this point. so he did a large operation: he doubled the salary, and assigned every delivery rabbit an (optimal) electronics recycling bin/regular trash place to search for phones.
It went quickly: they found a phone every four minutes of searching on average. in three months they found 1350 phones. of those, there were more than enough for each rabbit to take 20 phones.
RA arranged all of them, sorting from the best working to the least. He worked with old features on the working phones and built a simple compatibility operating system.
He installed the route app on all the devices, and gave it to the delivery rabbits. project delivery phones done.
When a new delivery request was sent to the company, it would automatically send a letter to the right delivery rabbit.
for the first years it worked good. but then the days darkened, and rabbits started stealing the carrots.
They read the letters and take the carrots instead of the rabbit that request them. they even built a company called "evil.corp" out of the profits.
RA first attempt was to encrypt the message. he installed on all of the phones a program to decode the text using a builtin key. it didnt work .

evil.corp still read the messages, but they searched for messages that looks encrpyed. they didnt know whats written there , but they followed that delivery rabbit and take the carrots from the poor rabbit.

RA thought about this for a week. it seems impossible: he need to have undetectable letters. sure, he could embed something like lemon secret writing, but it would be easy to detect, and evil.corp likely even tought about this before him.

So, impossible letters. every one of the rabbits already gets a lot of letters. he considered sending constantly, every 10-40 minutes messages to all of the delivery team, but it would overload the slow mail system
in additional to exposing every delivery rabbit constantly.
in the next day he thought about somthing brillent.
"wait. each of the delivery team alredy getting a lot of mail. what if the letter I would send would look exactly 1:1 as the rest? "

at first, he thought about embedding the secret as letters: the first char of the first word, second of the second and so on (and back to the first letter after the end). unfutunally, it was too limiting and did not generate sensable sentences:
"I love rabbits and have given some very nice handmade home made spider baskets come early September each winter when rabbit activity often starts around mid November after the young goats return"
(when he tried to start with "I love rabbits and")
"but, what about spesific word choices?". and so, he started the project
first, he assigned every word in rabbitish an index. then took 2,000 of messages he considered just normal. he wrote a simple program in his phone,
that assign every word an array with 52,000 random numbers, and starts to walk down the words, trying to predict the next word.
if there was "I AM WALKING ", the algorithm would change the numbers so I+AM would be closer to the value of WALKING
at first, the predictions were terrable, but as more letters flow in, it started changing
eventually, he ends up with an algorithm that write a list of words and how reasonable they would come next, like so

so, he wrote a simple encode/decode from this LLM choices. it choses a "normal" prompt for that. then he installed a program that alredy have the pre-trained arrays on all phones, and sent the letters. they looked exactly like the
the rest of the letters so evil.corp didnt notice.
later, there was a problem of traitors in the compony, so he choose a different parameters for each one of the rabbits so delivery rabbits couldnt look even at each other letters.

RA was 16 here. he created the delivery company because his family always told him to bring carrots to "friends of the family", and if that's not enough they ask him to bring carrots to their friends, since he's already on the way...
